title: Gandhari
hook: her son comes to her for a blessing before battle, and Gandhari will not say the words he wants

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti walked out of the city with the kingdom won, guiding Gandhari, whose hand rested on her shoulder. Did you offer a hand to someone hard to walk beside? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-nine.

A mother's blessing, before a fight, is supposed to be easy. Go well. Come home. Win. During the war, the Mahabharata says, Duryodhana came to his mother Gandhari and asked for her blessing for victory. He was her son. He was fighting for his life and his crown. All she had to say was, may you win. She never said it. Today Gandhari gets her own days, starting with the words she gave him instead.
screen: `A SON ASKS FOR A BLESSING.` → `MAY YOU WIN.` → `SHE NEVER SAID IT.`

segments.voice: Her answer is a short line in Sanskrit: yato dharmas tato jayah. Where dharma is, there is victory. It's a blessing that refuses to take sides by name. If Duryodhana is in the right, it's a blessing. If he isn't, it's a warning. Gandhari doesn't tell him which. She lets the line do its work. And this wasn't the first time she said hard things to him. Before the war, in the Book of Effort, she is called into the royal court while Krishna's peace mission is failing. She speaks to her son in front of everyone, here in paraphrase. A person who can't rule his own senses can't rule a kingdom for long. Make peace with your cousins. She speaks hard words to her husband too, for letting their son go so far. Duryodhana walks out of the hall. Put the two scenes together. First, it's a mother's love with a spine. She doesn't stop being his mother; she stops flattering him. Second, it's honest about limits. She can't make him listen. She can only refuse to say what isn't true. Third, the line outlives the story. After the war, when grief makes her want to curse the victors, the epic reminds her of her own words: where dharma is, there is victory. The answer she gave her son at the hardest hour comes back to steady her own hand.
screen: `WHERE DHARMA IS, THERE IS VICTORY` · `A BLESSING THAT NAMES NO SIDE` · `SHE WARNS HIM IN OPEN COURT` · `HER OWN WORDS COME BACK TO HER`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: the honest blessing. Sit comfortably and let the breath slow. Bring to mind someone you love who is pushing hard for something right now. Notice the easy blessing you'd like to give: go on, you'll win. Then ask, gently: what would I wish for them if I wished for what's right, not just for what they want? Let that wish take shape, in your own plain words. You don't have to say it to them. Just hold it for a few breaths. If you pray, you can pray it for them. The bell holds the time.
Gandhari. Asked by her son for a blessing of victory, she said only: where dharma is, there is victory. Today's word.
Your line: Gandhari. Today, when someone asks you to cheer them on, give an honest blessing instead of an easy one, the way Gandhari did. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-nine.

howItsDone: Hindus hear Gandhari's words in retellings of the Mahabharata, and some Hindus still quote the phrase yato dharmas tato jayah.

original.note: Sanskrit: where dharma is, there is victory. Gandhari's answer to Duryodhana.

trapdoor: what you thought: a mother always blesses her son to win.
what it means: Gandhari's blessing names no side: where dharma is, there is victory.
what a scholar hears: after the war the epic recalls her words to her when grief moves her to curse the Pandavas.

notes: Confirm the Stri Parva passage: Vyasa (or the narrator) recalls that during the war Duryodhana asked Gandhari's blessing each day and she answered 'yato dharmas tato jayah', and this is recalled to restrain her anger at the Pandavas. Check who recalls it and the section number.
Confirm the Udyoga Parva court scene: Gandhari summoned; she reproaches Dhritarashtra and tells Duryodhana that one who cannot master his senses cannot keep a kingdom; Duryodhana leaves.
The phrase also appears elsewhere in the Mahabharata; the script ties it only to Gandhari's answer.
